sources_read: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 8 (#7) and Internal Quality Checks row 8 (#7, no extra annotation)
rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/test.sh and tests/tools (diffed against the task: identical)

qc/runs/coldwater-strict-2026-10-02-r13/raw-evidence-index.json; recomputed SHA256 of run_golden.sh and the seven results/*.json (all match); recomputed SHA256 of hosted Oracle verifier/reward.json and of the Luna gates/reward-details.json (both match)
evidence: The brief asks for a product that cannot be met by a static page, a single CRUD screen or a mock. instruction.md: 'there is no starter app to finish'; environment/Dockerfile creates /app with only .gitkeep, and seed_data.json holds 'snippets': [] with no starter implementation, so there is nothing to tweak. The smallest conforming submission needs (ui.md) an own text model with caret, selection, multi-caret, undo/redo, find/replace, token colouring and a formatter, with textarea/contenteditable and ready-made editors forbidden; (behaviour.md, security.md) an isolated preview with console capture, error line numbers, a five-second budget, Stop, last-good restore and refusal of dynamic evaluation; (integration.md) an Express server with SQLite revisions that survive a process restart, stale-save refusal, idempotent restore and live library refresh across tabs. The golden is about 104 KB of hand-written source (custom-editor.js 49 KB, runtime.ts 27 KB, app.tsx 18 KB, server.js 9 KB). The reward path matches the ask: score.py returns 0 unless both gates pass and functional exceeds the 0.05 floor. The render gate needs real typing to show in the editor, the constraints gate fails a textarea/input/contenteditable document and requires a saved record to be read back after origin storage was cleared (so browser-only storage fails), and the floor needs more than 2.925 of 58.5 functional weight (functional/judge.toml weights summed by hand). I read all 42 functional criteria: every refusal or suppression criterion carries a positive control (for example cw_dynamic_code_refused 'it must run normally and log the marker, as the working control'; cw_stop_cancels_pending_work 'Fails ... if the control marker never appeared'; cw_format_error_keeps_draft 'or if the valid control did not format'; cw_stale_save_keeps_draft 'If B's Save was accepted ... this criterion fails'), so a dead feature gains no credit for doing nothing. Run evidence: hosted run on an EARLIER candidate gives Oracle 0.9833, nop 0 and a target-model app 0 (render 0.0, constraints 1.0); scripted golden on these bytes passes 3 gate, 42 functional and 6 polish checks. Risk is true because no nop, weak-app or configured-judge reward has been measured on these bytes, and the render gate was reduced to load-and-type since the hosted run, which makes the floor and the positive controls the only barrier between a thin app and a non-zero reward; that barrier is unmeasured. Two bounded observations, neither a row-7 defect: (a) a thin but genuine app (plain own-DOM editor with undo, unsandboxed iframe Run, server save) could pass both gates and roughly six weight units of functional criteria (cw_custom_typing_and_line_join, cw_long_line_editing, cw_basic_run_output, cw_html_preview, cw_console_levels_in_order, cw_run_starts_fresh_document), clear the floor at about 0.10 functional and then collect the visual and part of the polish weight, my estimate about 0.2 to 0.3 total; this is shaped partial credit for real work under the template weights, not a stub reward. (b) the constraints criterion allows 'A small input or textarea that is used only to receive keyboard or clipboard events', and does not bound what that hidden field holds, so an off-screen textarea holding the whole document with a mirrored div would pass the gate while borrowing native caret, selection and undo; it still has to build multi-caret, formatting, colouring, the runtime and revision storage, so real build work remains, and the gate-strictness question belongs to the constraint and anti-shortcut rows.
